LogicSwitch.on: FLOW_VERSION · requested AUTHORING_SCOPE line(s) · EXECUTION_READY · GATE_QUEUE · blast radius

LogicSwitch: - WHEN `FLOW_VERSION=v1` AND the request's blast radius reaches the legacy v1 `tasks/` layout or task-ID rewriting -> READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/migration-v1-v2.directive.xml") (live v1→v2 migration; returns when the repo is v2) - WHEN any requested scaffold target has `AUTHORING_SCOPE= READY=no|not-applicable` -> STOP with that target's exact `AUTHORING_SCOPE_DIAG` and `AUTHORING_SCOPE_NEXT`; the named owning spec flow remains allowed to repair evidence, but scaffold never edits it - WHEN every requested scaffold target has `AUTHORING_SCOPE= READY=yes` -> continue scaffold authoring; unrelated red scope lines and aggregate `AUTHORING_READY=no` do not block a narrower target set; missing runtime gates are declared bootstrap work, not a reason to load readiness setup - WHEN `EXECUTION_READY=no` AND the ticket/phase about to run is itself the exact owner listed in `GATE_QUEUE` -> continue only that phase: `sdd-task --phase` and `sdd-verify --task … --phase …` independently derive the setup exemption; it expires when the ticket is no longer TODO/IN_PROGRESS - WHEN `EXECUTION_READY=no` AND the request would execute any other product/library phase -> STOP: work the exact `GATE_QUEUE` first; a missing/vacuous runtime gate can never authorize product execution - WHEN `GATE_QUEUE_DIAG: infra-спека … одобрена, тикетов пока нет …` is printed (kind `infra-spec-no-tickets`) -> tell the operator that infra scope has no tickets yet and point at the `/sdd-scaffold` skill to cut them — a separate process, never READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE'd from here (scaffold itself hands off back into this flow, so loading it in-place would cycle) - WHEN `GATE_QUEUE_DIAG: область тикета … не совпала с порталом … (похожие имена)` is printed (kind `scope-name-mismatch`) -> fix the mismatch directly — edit the ticket's `Scope:` field or the portal scope name (whichever is the typo), never both by guesswork; not a reason to load another directive - WHEN `FLOW_VERSION=v1` AND the request's blast radius stays inside its own legacy scope (`AX_PREFLIGHT_BLAST_RADIUS_SCOPED`) -> record state in one line and continue the legacy-compatible owner flow; do not reinterpret v1 with v2 authoring fields - WHEN `EXECUTION_READY=yes` AND the request is execute -> continue execution - DEFAULT -> continue the non-scaffold, non-execution owner flow without reinterpreting either readiness fact
